correctness.rationale: With odd/even D1=diag(B,b), D2=diag(b,B) and migration matrix P(d)=[[1-d,cd],[cd,1-d]], the two-season transfer is (J P(d) D1)^2. Its one-season positive square root Perron root equals lambda_max of symmetric [[cdB,sqrt(Bb)(1-d)],[sqrt(Bb)(1-d),cdb]], giving Lambda(d)=[cd(B+b)+sqrt(c^2d^2(B-b)^2+4Bb(1-d)^2)]/2. The radicand is squared Euclidean norm of the affine vector (u*d,v*(1-d)) with u=c(B-b)>0,v=2sqrt(Bb)>0, which is strictly convex on [0,1]; hence every interior d loses to the endpoint chord. Endpoints are sqrt(Bb) and cB, giving exact c*=sqrt(b/B), with just endpoints tied at equality. Differentiating the norm twice gives g=u^2v^2/g^3 and the stated uniform strong-convexity penalty. Independently checked Decimal parameter examples (B,b)=(4,1), c=1/4,1/2,3/4: exact winners d=0,both endpoints,d=1; all sample interiors are inferior. Real-parameter universality rests on analytic strict convexity, not sampled values.
